intro: You're looking for a partnership accountant near you, likely because you're part of a partnership that needs its accounts and returns prepared, or you're thinking of setting one up. A partnership accountant can handle the yearly accounts, the partnership return, and make sure each partner's profit share is correctly reflected on their own tax return. We introduce you to a suitable UK accountant who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a partnership accountant usually need
need_lead: Most people searching for a partnership accountant near them are dealing with one of these situations.
needs: You are in a business partnership and need the annual partnership accounts and return prepared accurately.
You want to make sure each partner's share of profits is correctly allocated to their individual tax returns.
You are forming a partnership and need advice on how the partnership agreement should set out profit shares.
You are unsure how basis period reform affects your partnership and need guidance on the transition.
You need an accountant who understands partnerships and can help you meet your filing obligations without last-minute stress.
context_heading: One key thing to understand about partnership accounting
context: In a partnership, the business itself doesn't pay income tax; instead, each partner is taxed on their share of the profits through their own self assessment return. The partnership must still file a partnership return with HMRC, and the way profits are shared is usually set out in the partnership agreement. A partnership accountant prepares the partnership accounts and return and allocates profits correctly to each partner's tax return.

It's also worth knowing that the word "accountant" isn't protected in the UK, so anyone can call themselves one. Protected titles like Chartered Accountant or Chartered Certified Accountant show the holder is bound by a professional body's ethics, training and complaints rules. Every accountancy practice must also be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, so you can ask which body supervises them.

faqs.q: Do I need a separate accountant for each partner's tax return?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Many partnership accountants also prepare the individual partners' self assessment returns, but you can choose to have separate accountants if you prefer. It's worth asking what's included in the quote.

faqs.q: What is basis period reform and does it affect my partnership?
faqs.a: Basis period reform changes how unincorporated businesses, including partnerships, are taxed on their profits, moving to a tax-year basis. If your accounting period doesn't align with the tax year, you may need to apportion profits. An accountant can explain how this applies to your partnership.

faqs.q: Can a partnership accountant help if we don't have a written partnership agreement?
faqs.a: Yes, they can still prepare the accounts and return, but without a written agreement, profit sharing may default to equal shares under partnership law. It's often sensible to put an agreement in place, and an accountant can discuss the tax implications with you.

faqs.q: How are accountants supervised for anti-money-laundering?
faqs.a: Accountancy practices must be supervised by a professional body or by HMRC for anti-money-laundering purposes. You can ask which body supervises the firm you're considering, and it's a reasonable question to ask before engaging them.
